data.hypothesis: Fusing the forward and input-gradient work into one launch should save launch overhead and reuse output coordinates, input bounds checks, and filter-base setup. The shared loop adds a second accumulator and loads for both paths, so register pressure or reduced occupancy may offset those savings; complete-call timing is needed to determine the result.
data.notes: The supplied baseline is correct and measured at 0.035464 s mean over three samples. No fused-candidate measurement is available yet; the controller must validate correctness and compare complete-call timing. The weight-gradient kernel and its execution path are unchanged.
transformations: Replace separate forward and input-gradient launches with one fused kernel.
Share output-coordinate calculation, filter-base setup, and zero-padding bounds checks while preserving each accumulation order and fresh writes to both outputs.
Keep the weight-gradient kernel and launch unchanged.
